annotation.title_clean: Proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act) – Consolidated compromise amendments (IMCO/LIBE)
annotation.title_en: Proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on harmonised rules on Artificial Intelligence (Artificial Intelligence Act) – Consolidated compromise amendments (IMCO/LIBE)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament, Committee on the Internal Market and Consumer Protection (IMCO) and Committee on Civil Liberties, Justice and Home Affairs (LIBE); Rapporteurs Benifei, B. & Tudorache, I.-D.
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament IMCO/LIBE consolidated compromise amendments to the Commission's AI Act proposal (COM(2021)0206), excerpting notified bodies, standards, common specifications, conformity assessment, CE marking, registration, and AI literacy. It reinforces third-party and internal-control conformity assessment for high-risk AI, with limited machinery and physical-product provisions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Member States designate notifying authorities and notified bodies that must be independent, competent, cybersecure and insured.
Harmonised standards and Commission common specifications give a presumption of conformity for high-risk AI and foundation models.
Conformity assessment is by internal control or via a notified body; for products under Annex II legislation, such as machinery, it is integrated into the sectoral assessment.
Physical high-risk AI systems carry a physical CE marking, and digital-only systems carry a digital one; certificates are valid up to four years.
High-risk systems and foundation models must be registered in a public EU database; an AI literacy obligation is introduced.
